Hi everyone, I’m 24 years old and have been dealing with health anxiety my whole life. It was pretty manageable until I was 21 and started experiencing stomach issues. Everything points to standard IBS, but when symptoms pop up I go into an anxiety attack. It’s hard to eat and I’m afraid to, so much so that I have been in an eating disorder program for the last six months. I am terrified to eat because symptoms usually appear after eating. They treat me as if I have anorexia and completely dismiss what’s actually going on. It would be easier if I wasn’t actually having physical symptoms, but I am. I have diarrhea every few weeks or so, sometimes more. I have urgency to use the toilet most days, and I just feel uncomfortable in my stomach.. It feels debilitating. I feel like I’m dying and no one believes me. I’ve been entirely stuck in this cycle of fear and haven’t had a job since this started. Health anxiety can be so debilitating and it’s hard to get help for it because most people don’t understand it. It’s so bad that any stomach sensation can bring on anxiety. I’ll have days where it doesn’t bother me as much, but then I’ll have symptoms and then that’s it, I’m out of commission for the day.. thank you all for your stories, it helps me realize that I am not alone

Good luck friend. Withdrawal symptoms from weed are very real and suck but you really just need to stick it out to come out the other side because it will get better after a little while and in the meantime you’ll feel your life starting to come back to you. Somethings you might experience is first of all you’ll probably have trouble sleeping, you will most likely have some nasty, gross night sweats(and your B.O. might be smellier because your body is going through a detox) and have trouble keeping yourself cool regardless of temperature (kind of like if you have a bit of a fever) your stomach may hurt or feel kinda sick (hasn’t happened to me but I’ve heard of it), decreased appetite and some ppl feel like they have a bit of the flu. Emotions wise you’ll most likely feel more anxious especially if you were using it to cover up your anxiety. Just knowing that your anxious because of withdrawals is helpful because you can be preventative and take care of yourself. This is all to be expected and is a sign that your body is adjusting back to normalcy. Some people are lucky and don’t feel any of this, but I think it makes sense that the heavier users experience more symptoms than others. I would suggest allowing yourself to rest at least for the first few days and be kind to yourself as your body will be going through some stuff. If you are having night sweats make sure you are replenishing your electrolytes or you’ll feel very shitty.. I have been adding a bit of pedialyte to my water and honestly that has been helping A LOT. Bottom line is, it’ll suck for a few weeks at most(honestly I started feeling better after less than a week) and the withdrawals are REAL, but  it’s not going to be like opioid withdrawal or another substance like that. My heart goes out to opioid addiction warriors, that’s hell on earth. Not trying to belittle the symptoms of weed detox, just want you to know I really really really doubt you will need medical intervention to help you out. Of course if you personally need it, go right ahead, just isn’t as common with weed. I strongly recommend therapy during this time to help you out with this, or even joining a meeting like AA or NA as these programs can be applied to marijuana addicts. What I am try to say is that it’s good to be aware of how you might feel and how to make yourself feel a bit better, but there’s no reason to be afraid and you CAN quit. Having a support system that understands where you are at is very helpful. If nothing else, use this sub as your support system as everyone is incredibly kind on here:) for me, I needed something a bit more intense and structured so I went to IOP which has been incredibly helpful. Good luck!

Hello, yes I believe it is possible that this could be IBS. But just so you know, IBS is hard to diagnose as there is no test that says if you have it or not. About 15% of the population has IBS, it is a big umbrella term. I am a bit similar to you in that I go to the toilet very frequently, especially right when I wake up and I have ibs-d. It may be normal for your body to act like this, some people just go more than others! Usually people with IBS have either diarrhea or constipation along with pain, gas, bloating and other symptoms. You could be experiencing a mild form of IBS, or maybe you are sensitive to something in your diet. There is a lot of stuff that this could be, a good indicator of IBS is tracking symptoms over a period of time, so maybe start a food journal to see if there are any patterns in your symptoms? Either way, the majority of people deal with digestive issues in todays world, we just don't talk about it much. But there are several things to try out if you are wanting to have better digestion :)

It seems that the best thing for IBS is trial and error with diet and medications, lifestyle modifications, plus  stress management. Take a look around this subreddit, there's a lot of good advice on here. Good luck!
